latest_release.name: Voxt v2.1.1
latest_release.body:
### Requirements

- A Mac with Apple silicon and macOS 15 or later.

### Install

- Open Voxt-2.1.1-arm64.dmg and drag Voxt to Applications. It replaces Voxt 1.x there.
- Later versions install inside Voxt: choose Check for Updates… in the Voxt menu, then Install Update and Relaunch.


### Added

- **Meetings label the other side as Speaker 1, 2, 3 and so on**: with MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize installed, Voxt uses it after a meeting to transcribe the other side with speaker labels while your lines stay Me, before transcript correction and the summary. Long meetings go to it in pieces, so dictation waits at most one piece, and a voice keeps its number across the pieces. In a language MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize does not know (it knows Chinese and English), or when the language is left automatic so it cannot be told, the meeting keeps the selected model's transcription. Without it, the meeting works as before and its details link to Speech models.
- **Copy and edit notes in place, and see their source app**: each note has Copy and Edit buttons. Save writes the edit back to the note, and Cancel leaves it unchanged. If Voxt knows the frontmost app at capture time, new notes show its name.
- **Reopen recent cards from the menu bar**: the new Reopen card section lists up to five Rewrite or Translate conversations from the last 24 hours whose current answer was not inserted. Open one to continue with all its turns, including after restarting Voxt. With the menu bar icon off, the Dock menu has the same list. Deleting or clearing history removes its rows. Turning off Keep a history hides the list, and Settings → Privacy now says so.
- **Dictionary profiles**: keep named sets of dictionary entries for different situations. Existing entries move into the active Default profile with their meaning unchanged. Create, rename, delete, and switch profiles on the Dictionary page; Transcribe, Translate, and Rewrite use only the active profile. Hammerspoon, macOS Shortcuts, and shell scripts can switch without opening the Dictionary page by running `open -g 'voxtnew://dictionary/profile?name=Work'`. See docs/dictionary-profiles.md.
- **Rewrite's answer card renders Markdown** (#4119): the language model answers in Markdown, and the card now shows a Rewrite answer as it reads — headings, bold, lists, code, and a formula's TeX — instead of the raw markers, the way the chat apps show replies, while it streams in and in a conversation's answers. What you said stays as written. Copy and Insert still use the answer's original text.
- **Wait for the language model offers presets up to 60 minutes**: the setting on the Language models page now offers Automatic, 1, 2, 5, 10, 30 and 60 minutes, and No limit, replacing the Custom… minutes field. A custom wait saved by an earlier version keeps its duration and shows as what it is.
- **Voxt 2 installs updates inside the app** (#3961): release builds check Voxt 2's signed stable or beta feed, download the update, install it and relaunch, as Voxt 1.x did. Settings → Diagnostics & About keeps the automatic check, beta and automatic install controls. Builds without a feed still check GitHub and point to the download.
- **Update announcements are shorter**: the current version's announcement appears once after an update, with a title and at most three short lines. **What's new** opens the full notes, also available any time in Settings → About → Updates.
- **Dictionary highlights in Transcribe**: the Try preview and answer card highlight recognised text that matches an enabled dictionary term or alias.
- **Pick an accent color and make the window transparent** (#4123, #4180): Settings → Appearance has a Color picker with a light and a dark preview, and Reset color goes back to the default teal. Buttons, the selected sidebar item, the recording window and the answer card follow the color. Blog | Documentation | Quick Start | Cookbook | SGLang | Join Slack

⭐ Star SGLang-Omni to help more builders discover open infrastructure for multimodal and speech serving!

## News - [2026/11] 🎙️ [Voxt 2.0](./Voxt/README.md) redefines open-source voice interaction on Mac: voice input, any-to-any translation, and a local AI assistant, with a 92% shorter wait after long dictation than 1.x. \[[Download](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-omni/releases/download/voxt-v2.1.1/Voxt-2.1.1-arm64.dmg)\] \[[Changelog](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-omni/blob/main/Voxt/CHANGELOG.md)\] - [2026/11] 🔁 OpenRSI × SGLang-Omni: recursive self-improvement (RSI) scaled to production AI infrastructure, with 14 merged PRs across 8 speech and omni models and +7.6% to +326.5% throughput on H100. \[[Blog](https://index.openrsi.foundation/blog/2026/openrsi-sglang-omni/)\] - [2026/10] 🗺️ A unified runtime for interactive intelligence: native full-duplex models, turn-based multimodal models, and cascaded systems, coordinated through composable graphs and persistent sessions. \[[Blog](https://www.sglang.io/blog/omni-interactive-runtime)\] - [2026/10] 🚀 SGLang-Omni **v0.2.0** is on [PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/sglang-omni/). Install with `uv pip install --prerelease=allow "sglang-omni==0.2.0"`. \[[Installation](https://sgl-project.github.io/sglang-omni/get_started/installation.html)\] - [2026/10] 🐟 Day-0 support for [Fish Audio Drama 3](https://huggingface.co/fishaudio/drama-3): multi-speaker text-to-speech with voice cloning and natural-language control, streamed on `/v1/audio/speech`. \[[Blog](https://www.sglang.io/blog/spg-topology)\] \[[Cookbook](https://sgl-project.github.io/sglang-omni/cookbook/fishaudio_drama3.html)\] \[[Technical Report](https://github.com/fishaudio/fish-speech/tree/main/docs/assets/Fish_Audio_Drama_3_Technical_Report.pdf)\] - [2026/10] 🎙️ Introducing [Voxt](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-omni/tree/main/Voxt), an open-source voice input tool for Mac, now integrating SGLang-Omni for faster local speech recognition on Apple Silicon. Combine ASR with LLM-based text refinement and personal system prompts for accurate technical terminology and personalized voice input, with fully local or remote inference options. [[Download](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-omni/releases/download/voxt-v2.1.1/Voxt-2.1.1-arm64.dmg)][[Demo]](https://x.com/GenAI_is_real/status/2109419016205017181)
Earlier news - [2026/09] 🐧 Day-0 support for [AuK](https://huggingface.co/tencent/AuK) and [AuK-Flash](https://huggingface.co/tencent/AuK-Flash): text + voice instructions → 24 kHz speech on `/v1/audio/speech`, audio + editing instructions → edited speech on `/generate`. \[[Cookbook](https://sgl-project.github.io/sglang-omni/cookbook/auk.html)\] - [2026/08] 🎵 Day-0 support for [MiniMax Music 3](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-Music3): lyrics + caption → 32 kHz stereo song on `/v1/audio/speech`. \[[Cookbook](https://sgl-project.github.io/sglang-omni/cookbook/minimax_music3.html)\] - [2026/08] 🚀 TTS architecture refactor: shared pipeline state, engine construction, reference encoding, capability metadata, and vocoder scheduling. \[[Roadmap](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-omni/issues/985)\] \[[Blog](https://github.com/zhaochenyang20/Awesome-ML-SYS-Tutorial/blob/main/sglang/sglang-omni/tts-refactor.md)\] - [2026/06] 🔥 MOSS-TTS Local Transformer v1.5 on SGLang-Omni with native-streaming 48 kHz speech. \[[Blog](https://lmsys.org/blog/2026-06-17-moss-tts-local-v15/)\] \[[Cookbook](https://sgl-project.github.io/sglang-omni/cookbook/moss_tts_local.html)\] - [2026/06] 🔥 Higgs Audio v3 TTS for real-time, controllable speech. \[[Blog](https://lmsys.org/blog/2026-06-04-higgs-audio-v3-tts/)\] \[[Cookbook](https://sgl-project.github.io/sglang-omni/cookbook/higgs_tts.html)\]
## About SGLang-Omni is a multi-stage serving runtime for omni, speech, and TTS models. Its design target is multi-stage decoding: generation split across heterogeneous stages with different compute patterns, dependency structures, and resource needs. SGLang-Omni owns the pipeline topology, stage lifecycle, inter-stage transport, model-family integration layer, and OpenAI-compatible serving surface, while composing with [SGLang](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang) for high-performance autoregressive scheduling and model execution where applicable. - **Multi-stage runtime**: SGLang-Omni models generation as coordinated stages: preprocessing, encoders, autoregressive engines, talkers, decoders, vocoders, and aggregators. - **Stage-specialized scheduling**: Each stage runs behind a scheduler matched to its workload, from SGLang-backed autoregressive scheduling to lightweight preprocessing and streaming vocoder loops. - **Transport-aware execution**: A control plane coordinates requests while the relay data plane moves tensor payloads across shared-memory, NCCL, NIXL, and Mooncake backends. - **API surface**: OpenAI-compatible endpoints expose multimodal chat, speech generation, batch speech, streaming speech, uploaded voices, and transcription. ## What SGLang-Omni Serves - **Omni chat and speech**: [Qwen3-Omni](https://sgl-project.github.io/sglang-omni/cookbook/qwen3_omni.html), [MiniCPM-o 4.5](https://sgl-project.github.io/sglang-omni/cookbook/minicpm_o.html), [Ming-Omni](https://sgl-project.github.io/sglang-omni/cookbook/ming_omni.html), [Ming-3.0-audio-flash](https://sgl-project.github.io/sglang-omni/cookbook/ming3_audio.html) — multimodal understanding and text/audio replies. - **Native full-duplex conversation**: [MiniCPM-o 4.5](https://sgl-project.github.io/sglang-omni/cookbook/minicpm_o.html), [PersonaPlex](https://sgl-project.github.io/sglang-omni/cookbook/personaplex.html), [NemotronLabs VoiceChat](https://sgl-project.github.io/sglang-omni/cookbook/nemotron_voicechat.html) — live listening and speaking over `/v1/realtime`, including camera input with MiniCPM-o. [Full-duplex guide](https://sgl-project.github.io/sglang-omni/developer_reference/full_duplex_guide.html). - **Cascaded voice assistants**: Compose ASR → LLM → TTS services into streaming, turn-based conversations with voice activity detection, conversation history, turn taking, and interruption. [Streaming cascade guide](https://sgl-project.github.io/sglang-omni/developer_reference/full_duplex_guide.html#streaming-cascade). - **Image and video generation**: [LLaDA2.0-Uni](https://sgl-project.github.io/sglang-omni/cookbook/llada2_uni.html) for text/image understanding, image generation, and editing; [Cosmos3 Nano](https://sgl-project.github.io/sglang-omni/cookbook/cosmos3_nano.html) for interleaved understanding and generation, with native image, video, and action routes. - **Music generation**: [MiniMax Music 3](https://sgl-project.github.io/sglang-omni/cookbook/minimax_music3.html) and [YuE2](https://sgl-project.github.io/sglang-omni/cookbook/yue2.html) — lyrics + style → stereo song, at 32 kHz and 48 kHz respectively. - **Speech generation**: [Higgs Audio v3](https://sgl-project.github.io/sglang-omni/cookbook/higgs_tts.html), [MOSS-TTS](https://sgl-project.github.io/sglang-omni/cookbook/moss_tts.html), [MOSS-TTS Local](https://sgl-project.github.io/sglang-omni/cookbook/moss_tts_local.html), [Fish Audio Drama 3](https://sgl-project.github.io/sglang-omni/cookbook/fishaudio_drama3.html), [Fish Speech S2-Pro](https://sgl-project.github.io/sglang-omni/cookbook/fishaudio_s2_pro.html), [Qwen3-TTS](https://sgl-project.github.io/sglang-omni/cookbook/qwen3_tts.html), [Fun-CosyVoice3](https://sgl-project.github.io/sglang-omni/cookbook/fun_cosyvoice3.html), [Voxtral TTS](https://sgl-project.github.io/sglang-omni/cookbook/voxtral_tts.html), [Ming-Omni-TTS](https://sgl-project.github.io/sglang-omni/cookbook/ming_tts.html), [Ming-3.0-TTS](https://sgl-project.github.io/sglang-omni/cookbook/ming3_tts.html), [dots.tts](https://sgl-project.github.io/sglang-omni/cookbook/dots_tts.html), [ZONOS2](https://sgl-project.github.io/sglang-omni/cookbook/zonos2.html) — `/v1/audio/speech`, with batch, streaming, and voice features varying by model. - **Instruction-driven speech generation and editing**: [AuK and AuK-Flash](https://sgl-project.github.io/sglang-omni/cookbook/auk.html) — text and voice instructions → speech; audio and editing instructions → edited speech. - **Audio transcription**: [Qwen3-ASR](https://sgl-project.github.io/sglang-omni/cookbook/qwen3_asr.html), [Fun-ASR](https://sgl-project.github.io/sglang-omni/cookbook/fun_asr.html), [ARK-ASR](https://sgl-project.github.io/sglang-omni/cookbook/arkasr.html), [Nemotron 3.5 ASR](https://sgl-project.github.io/sglang-omni/cookbook/nemotron3_5_asr.html), [Nemotron Transcribe](https://sgl-project.github.io/sglang-omni/cookbook/nemotron_transcribe.html), [Ming-3.0-ASR](https://sgl-project.github.io/sglang-omni/cookbook/ming3_asr.html), experimental [Whisper](https://sgl-project.github.io/sglang-omni/cookbook/whisper_asr.html), and [MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize](https://sgl-project.github.io/sglang-omni/cookbook/moss_transcribe_diarize.html) via `/v1/audio/transcriptions`. MOSS-TD also returns speaker labels and timestamps (`response_format=verbose_json`). - **Speaker diarization**: [Nemotron 3 Diarization](https://sgl-project.github.io/sglang-omni/cookbook/nemotron_diarization.html) — speaker intervals for uploaded recordings and live audio, including overlapping speech. - **Speech translation**: [Hy-SimulMT](https://sgl-project.github.io/sglang-omni/cookbook/hy_simulmt.html) — Chinese speech → English text and English speech → Chinese text, with file and realtime translation. See the [audio translation guide](https://sgl-project.github.io/sglang-omni/basic_usage/audio_translations.html) for endpoint and model support. ## Hardware Support | Backend | Status | Notes | |---------|--------|-------| | **NVIDIA CUDA** | Supported | Default backend with full model coverage. | | **Apple Silicon** | Experimental | Qwen3-ASR runs through Torch MPS on macOS arm64. Install with [`install.sh`](./install.sh) and follow the [Qwen3-ASR guide](./docs/cookbook/qwen3_asr.md#apple-silicon). | | **Intel GPU (XPU)** | Supported | Intel Arc GPUs via PyTorch XPU. **Qwen3-ASR, Whisper ASR, Fun-ASR-Nano, Nemotron 3.5 ASR, MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize, Qwen3-TTS, Fun-CosyVoice3, ZONOS2, Audar-TTS, Qwen3-Omni, MiniMax Music 3, MiniCPM-o, Ming-Omni, Ming-Omni-TTS, Nemotron VoiceChat, PersonaPlex, AuK/AuK-Flash and dots.tts serve end-to-end**. The [Intel XPU guide](./docs/other_platforms/installation_xpu.md) has the install steps, each model's launch command and how many cards it needs; the backend is auto-detected. | Additional model guides, including experimental and research-oriented paths, are available in the [Cookbook](https://sgl-project.github.io/sglang-omni/). ## Quick Start - [Installation](https://sgl-project.github.io/sglang-omni/get_started/installation.html) - [TTS usage](https://sgl-project.github.io/sglang-omni/basic_usage/tts.html) - [ASR cookbook](https://sgl-project.github.io/sglang-omni/cookbook/qwen3_asr.html) ## Community & Support SGLang-Omni welcomes contributors working on inference systems, kernels, scheduling, inter-stage communication, model runners and cache efficiency, model integration, benchmarking, production deployment. Join the [SGLang Slack](https://slack.sglang.io) or read the [developer reference](https://sgl-project.github.io/sglang-omni/developer_reference/main.html). Organizations interested in supporting SGLang-Omni, TTS, or omni model serving can contact Chenyang Zhao at [zhaochenyang@lmsys.org](mailto:zhaochenyang@lmsys.org). ## Citation If you use SGLang-Omni for your research, please cite our technical blogs on the [unified interactive runtime](https://www.sglang.io/blog/omni-interactive-runtime) and the [Stage--Process--GPU topology](https://www.sglang.io/blog/spg-topology): ```bibtex @misc{sglangomniinteractive2026, title={Unified Runtime for Full-Duplex Interactive Intelligence with {SGLang Omni}}, author={{SGLang-Omni Team}}, howpublished={\url{https://www.sglang.io/blog/omni-interactive-runtime}}, year={2026}, month={oct} } @misc{sglangomni2026, title={Fish Audio Drama 3 Meets {SGLang-Omni}: Day-0 Support and the Stage--Process--GPU Topology}, author={{SGLang-Omni Team}}, howpublished={\url{https://www.sglang.io/blog/spg-topology}}, year={2026}, month={oct} } ``` ## Acknowledgments SGLang-Omni builds on the SGLang ecosystem and on open model work from the TTS, speech, and omni-model communities. We thank the model teams, systems contributors, and partner organizations helping make open multimodal serving faster, more reliable, and easier to extend.
